nodes.description: In the multisystem patient's fibroblasts and lymphoblasts, reduced MCAT produced a combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency - reduced complex I (NDUFB8), II (SDHB) and IV (COXII) subunits with correspondingly decreased respiratory-chain enzyme activities - rescued by re-expressing wild-type MCAT. In that patient protein lipoylation was normal, and in a mutant myoblast line the p.Thr271Ile allele restored lipoylation but only partially restored respiration, implicating impaired respiratory-chain assembly rather than lipoylation as the relevant consequence. mtFAS's role here is the supply of acyl-ACP for complex assembly (via mitochondrial ACP/NDUFAB1), not fatty-acid synthesis as an end in itself.
